newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Feb 10.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

U.S. doctors have lost the battle to save nine-month old Matthew Eappen. The British nanny of the child, eighteen year old Louise Woodward from Cheshire who was accused of battering the baby, now faces first-degree murder charges.
AVIS EUROPE STEERS BACK TO UK LISTING
Europe's largest car hire company, Avis, after an absence of eight years, is to return to the London Stock Exchange in a flotation which is set to value it at about 700 million stg.

Figures published by the Bank of England have shown that gilt- edged market makers' profits have slumped by more than half. GEMMs operating profits in 1996 were just 11 million stg, down from 25 million in 1995.
BANK TO OPT FOR SOFTLY, SOFTLY APPROACH ON INDEXED GILTS

The Bank of England is not convinced by claims that index-linked debt might reduce the Treasury borrowing costs by hundreds of millions of pounds a year. So it is likely that it will raise the percentage of government borrowing it funds with index-linked gilts only gradually over a period of time.
PROPERTY CASH CALLS RAISING BEARS' HACKLES

There appears to be growing institutional unease that a flood of rights issues from the commercial property industry are on the way. Three of the sector's better-known names Land Securities, Great Portland and Ashquay have tapped the Square Mile for cash.
